questions.question: Which of the following indicators reflects inequality in the distribution of income among individuals in a population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lorenz Curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lorenz Curve is a graphical representation that illustrates the distribution of income or wealth among individuals or households in a population.
 
• It is used to measure income inequality, where the degree of deviation from the line of perfect equality (the diagonal line) indicates the level of inequality.
 
• The closer the Lorenz Curve is to the diagonal line, the more equal the income distribution; the farther it is, the greater the inequality.
 
• The curve is often used in conjunction with the Gini Coefficient, which quantifies the level of income inequality as a single numerical value.
 
• Developed by Max Lorenz in 1905, this tool remains a cornerstone in economic studies related to inequality and social welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gini Coefficient:**

 
 
• The Gini Coefficient is a numerical measure derived from the Lorenz Curve, ranging from 0 to 1.
 
• A Gini Coefficient of 0 indicates perfect equality, while a value of 1 indicates perfect inequality.
 
• It is widely used by economists and policymakers to compare income inequality across regions or countries.
 
 
 
• **Dependency Ratio:**
 
 
• This is a demographic metric that indicates the ratio of dependents (young and elderly) to the working-age population.
 
• While important for understanding economic pressures, it does not measure income inequality.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):**
 
 
• CPI measures changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households over time.
 
• It is a key indicator of inflation, not income distribution.
 
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• LFPR measures the proportion of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• It provides insights into labor market dynamics but does not reflect income inequality.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Income Inequality Studies:**
 
 
• The study of income inequality gained prominence during the 20th century as economists sought to understand its implications on economic growth and social stability.
 
• Tools like the Lorenz Curve and Gini Coefficient remain fundamental to these analyses.

questions.question: When 1 litre of water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its volume _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increases.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• In normal cases, the volume of substances increases on heating and decreases while cooling.
 
• When 1 litre of water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C volume of water will start **increasing** this due to water's unique property known as '**Anomalous Expansion of Water**'.
 
• Anomalous Expansion of Water occurs between 4°C to 0°C.
 
• **The density of water is a maximum at 4 °C.**
 
• When water is cooled from 4°C to 0°C, its density decreases.
 
• The anomalous expansion of water helps **preserve aquatic life during very cold weather**.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• When water reaches **4°C the molecules have been pushed as close** to one another as possible and the density of water becomes precisely **1.00 g/cm³**__
 
• When water **freezes at 0°C** due to the crystal structure the molecules arranged in some structured fashion so a little far apart ended up less dense - __0.93 g/cm__³ - and so **floats due to buoyancy.**

**As density decreases the volume increases.**

**Volume = mass /density.**

questions.question: What did the Supreme Court decide in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) about the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution of India?

options.text: The President of India has the ultimate authority to approve or reject constitutional amendments independently.
The Parliament cannot amend any part of the Constitution under any circumstances.
The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.
The Parliament has unlimited power to amend any part of the Constitution, including the Fundamental Rights.

questions.solution: The correct answer is __**The Parliament can amend the Constitution, but it cannot change or destroy its basic structure or essential features.**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala** case (1973) is one of the most significant judgments in Indian constitutional history. • The Supreme Court laid down the **"Basic Structure Doctrine"**, which restricts the power of the Parliament to amend the Constitution in a way that alters its fundamental structure. • According to the judgment, while the Parliament has the authority under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution to amend any part of the Constitution, it cannot alter or destroy its basic structure or essential features. • The basic structure includes principles such as the supremacy of the Constitution, separation of powers, fundamental rights, and the rule of law. • This doctrine ensures that the core principles of the Indian Constitution remain preserved, even as the Constitution evolves through amendments.

questions.question: Which of the following options correctly lists the composition of the State Executive in India?

options.text: Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
Governor, Deputy Minister and State Council of Advisors
Governor, Chief Minister and State Legislative Assembly members

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The State Executive** in India is composed of the **Governor, Chief Minister, and Council of Ministers**. These bodies collectively function to govern the state and implement policies and programs.
 
• **Governor:** The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and represents the President of India at the state level. The Governor ensures the state's administration aligns with constitutional provisions and provides assent to bills passed by the state legislature.
 
• **Chief Minister:** The Chief Minister is the head of the government in the state. They act as the executive leader of the state, responsible for implementing policies and ensuring the smooth functioning of the state administration.
 
• **Council of Ministers:** The Council of Ministers assists the Chief Minister in decision-making and policy implementation. They hold portfolios such as education, health, agriculture, and finance, ensuring comprehensive governance across all sectors.
 
• These three components work together under a parliamentary system of governance at the state level, ensuring that decisions are made democratically and implemented effectively.
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• Option 2 includes the President, which is incorrect as the President is the head of state for the nation, not part of the state executive.
 
• Option 3 mentions Deputy Ministers and State Council of Advisors, which are not part of the official composition of the state executive.
 
• Option 4 refers to State Legislative Assembly members, who are part of the legislative branch, not the executive branch.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Governor, Chief Minister, and Council of Ministers.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Governor:**

 
 
• The **Governor** is appointed by the President of India and serves as the constitutional head of the state. They act as a link between the state and the central government.
 
• The Governor’s responsibilities include granting assent to bills, appointing the Chief Minister, and dissolving the state legislative assembly during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the elected leader of the majority party in the state legislative assembly. They are responsible for forming the Council of Ministers and advising the Governor.
 
• The Chief Minister represents the state at the national level and plays a crucial role in policy formulation and implementation.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The **Council of Ministers** is composed of ministers responsible for various departments. They help the Chief Minister in executing policies and managing the state’s administration.
 
• These ministers are collectively responsible to the state legislature and work under the guidance of the Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **State Executive Functions:**
 
 
• The state executive ensures the implementation of laws passed by the state legislature and delivers governance to the citizens of the state.
 
• It plays a vital role in maintaining law and order, promoting economic growth, and ensuring social welfare programs are effectively executed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Governor’s Role:**

 
 
• The Governor acts as a guardian of the Constitution within the state, ensuring that the state government functions within constitutional limits.
 
• The Governor has the power to summon and dissolve the state legislative assembly, appoint the Chief Minister, and oversee the implementation of central policies in the state.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister’s Role:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister leads the Council of Ministers and is primarily responsible for policy decisions, budget preparation, and coordination among various departments.
 
• They act as the representative of the state in national matters and ensure the state's development aligns with the central government’s goals.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers’ Role:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers manages specific portfolios and ensures the implementation of policies, programs, and projects for the state’s growth and development.
 
• They are collectively responsible to the state legislature and play a crucial role in decision-making processes.

__
 
• The 1991 economic liberalisation in India was a landmark reform aimed at transforming the Indian economy by removing restrictions on **Industry and Trade**.
 
• It included measures like **abolishing industrial licensing** (except for a few industries), reducing import tariffs, and allowing foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• The reforms introduced **privatisation and deregulation**, reducing the monopoly of public sector enterprises in key industries.
 
• The **trade policy** was revamped to promote exports, reducing the heavy reliance on import substitution strategies.

• **Industrial Policy of 1991:** It removed the **License Raj**, introduced competition in sectors previously dominated by the public sector, and encouraged private and foreign investments.
 
• **Trade Reforms:** Import duties were significantly reduced, quantitative restrictions on imports were lifted, and export promotion measures were introduced to integrate India with the global economy.
